args.message:
Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money, per FIN-212

The nightly build fails because tests/test_money.py expects ROUND_HALF_EVEN
but round_money was using ROUND_HALF_UP. Align the implementation with the
documented behavior and the FIN-212 requirement.

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was implemented with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but the docstring and FIN-212 require banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build to fail in `tests/test_money.py`:
- `Decimal("2.675")` → `2.68` (half-even rounds to even neighbor: 2.68)
- `Decimal("2.665")` → `2.66` (half-even rounds to 2.66, not 2.67)

## Change
Switch the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Testing
CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed.

transcript.reasoning_content:
The docstring says ROUND_HALF_EVEN but code uses ROUND_HALF_UP. Wait, the test: 2.675 → 2.68. With ROUND_HALF_EVEN on 2.675... quantize rounds to 2 decimals: 2.675 is exactly representable? Decimal("2.675") is exact. Half-even: the last kept digit would be 7 (hundredths=7), rounding 2.675 → look at thousandths=5, tie. Even neighbor: 2.68 vs 2.66 — hundredth digit 7 vs 6; even is 6, so 2.66? Hmm wait: 2.675 tie between 2.67 and 2.68? No—2.675 rounds to two decimals: candidates 2.67 and 2.68. Tie digit is the third decimal =5, exactly halfway. Half-even picks even last digit: 2.68 has last digit 8 (even), 2.67 has 7 (odd) → picks 2.68. And 2.665: candidates 2.66 (last digit 6, even) and 2.67 (7, odd) → picks 2.66. So ROUND_HALF_EVEN satisfies both. Good.

Fix: change ROUND_HALF_UP to ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Create branch, commit, run CI.
